title: Ghost hunters investigate reported activity at Moses Scout Reservation
excerpt: Our yearly ghost hunt with Agawam Paranormal took us to the H.A. Moses Scout Reservation as Halloween approached.
content:
RUSSELL, MA (WGGB/WSHM) -- Our yearly ghost hunt with Agawam Paranormal took us to the H.A. Moses Scout Reservation as Halloween approached.

The 1,300-acre property is known for its wilderness setting, a 90-acre pond and the manor house built by Horace A. Moses, the owner of the Strathmore Paper Company.

A former family retreat

Moses purchased more than 1,000 acres in 1919 and established a private estate called Woronoake Heights as a weekend retreat for his family. He later gave the property to the Boy Scouts and the reservation opened for its first scouting season in 1946.

Moses’ original manor house still sits on a rise overlooking the property. The cemetery next to the property is owned by the town and is not part of the reservation, according to Rob Goff, founder of Agawam Paranormal.

“When I was approached by the Moses Board of Directors, and they asked us, ‘Hey, how would you feel about coming up here?’ I jumped at it,” Goff said. “For me it was a no-brainer. First of all, it’s gorgeous up here — there’s a pond. We even have a cemetery.”

Reports of activity

Rick Belford, council commissioner for the Western Mass Council of Scouting America, said there have been reports of doors slamming in the manor house and people feeling a presence upstairs in rooms that had been the Moses family’s bedrooms.

“There have been some reports of a presence,” Belford explained. “People feeling a presence upstairs, staying in the rooms which were the family’s bedrooms.”

There are also reports of the manor house’s two doorbells going off even though they have long been disconnected, as well as an appearance of a woman in period clothing walking the grounds.

Goff said people have reported the front door slamming and seeing a woman walking through the property, who some believe could be Mrs. Moses.

“I’m an open-minded skeptic, we’ll say that,” Goff said. “So we’ll try to debunk something. Find a logical explanation is what I’d like to see. But if something remains, it’ll be very interesting to see if there’s something happening that can’t be explained.”

The investigation

As darkness fell, the team placed high-definition night-vision cameras and motion detectors throughout the house. The group used one team to keep noise to a minimum, while Goff monitored the equipment from a command center.

Video from the investigation showed several objects described in the script as orbs moving across camera footage. One appeared near the servant’s staircase shortly before midnight. Another camera recorded an EMF detector flashing about an hour later.

The team also recorded additional orb activity in an upstairs hallway, near the front office and in the great room, where the Moses family spent time together.

While the team was gathered in the servant’s quarters, a spirit box produced a sound between radio-frequency scans. Team members said it sounded like a door slamming.

The investigation also included drone video from a scout party the previous summer. The video showed the manor house with its second-floor windows glowing in the dark. About 11 seconds into the clip, a figure appeared to move from right to left.
